checks.name: Every declared core identity plus selected MCP identity is registered without changing original names or input schemas
Duplicate and unknown tools fail registration before they acquire core authority
MCP hints retain external effect, one attempt and explicit MCP Scope policy
Original result body is preserved and a schema-valid unified provider result references it
Dynamic provider results must match the actual current execution, snapshot and source identity
Child resource leases append their actual original Grant references to the original call contract
Domain malformed results fail the shared result boundary
Private data under a dynamic surface name survives native JSON round trip as rejection evidence
Schema mutation is rejected before the original implementation runs
Revoked core Provider blocks direct named execution through the same Registry
Intrinsic Task controls also require the current main-owned Task generation

boundary: Registry, source/effect/Scope policies, uniform receipt and private-capture contract fixtures. Actual final Session and original Task/Journal execution are additionally asserted by phase5-production-smoke.
